findings.what: Training labels are assigned before the 90-day window closes
findings.evidence: 101 of 1200 rows (8.4%) are labeled 0 with fewer than 90 days observed; those rows carry 33% more MQLs than the rest (p_BH = 0.027)
findings.action: Label = NULL, not 0, when snapshot_date + 90d > today. Re-label the 101 affected rows and add the rule to the labeling job.
findings.cost: one rule in the labeling job
findings.expect: the next model is not taught that marketing-engaged accounts fail

findings.what: Accounts are being scored on information older than the feature window
findings.evidence: 102 of 300 scoring accounts have a snapshot over 180 days old; 218 are over 90 days, and every feature is a 90-day window
findings.action: Flag it on the row, do not block it — working hypothesis: still actionable. READOUT compares stale vs fresh conversion within each arm; if stale loses, the flag becomes a filter.
findings.cost: enrichment refresh on ~1/3 of the batch
findings.expect: reps stop calling a description of a company from two quarters ago

findings.what: The model's own arithmetic promises more conversions than the business sees
findings.evidence: predicted probabilities sum to 19.7 conversions across 300 accounts (6.55%), against a field rate the brief puts at 1-3% (i.e. 3-9 conversions)
findings.action: Do not publish probabilities to any user or Salesforce field. Use the score only for the disagreement analysis in RECONCILE.
findings.expect: nobody forecasts off a number that is 2-6x the observed rate

findings.what: The model's dashboard number is memory, not prediction
findings.evidence: on 1099 labelled rows, the model's top-90 converts at 31.1% when it scores rows it was trained on and 6.7% when it scores rows it never saw (out-of-fold) — against a 7.1% base and 7.3% for a random list (mean of 200). The graph's worklist converts at 12.2% with 213 contacts already sunk vs 486 for the old contact sort at the same rate
findings.action: Never show an in-sample rate to anyone. Every number about this model that reaches a manager comes from out-of-fold or forward-in-time scoring, and says which.
findings.cost: 0 — the OOF scores exist; it is a rule about which column to read
findings.expect: the VP sees 6.7%, not 31%, and asks the right question

findings.what: Conversions per hour cannot be estimated from this data at all — only randomised
findings.evidence: the same yield curve says 'call more' read as a rate (5 contacts converts at 13.6% vs 6.5% base) and 'never call twice' read as a cost (14 contacts per conversion at 1 vs 37 at 5), both on cells of 50+ accounts. Contact count is confounded with the intent the rep already observed, so every observational estimate of hours-ROI is uninterpretable
findings.action: Do not compute or report conversions-per-hour from historical CRM data, in any cut. The arms in BUDGET are the measuring instrument, not a side experiment: randomised assignment is the only thing that makes the denominator readable.
findings.cost: 0 — it is a decision not to publish a number that is already being computed
findings.expect: the team stops justifying effort with a statistic that rises because effort was spent, which is the mechanism that killed the previous scoring effort

findings.what: At today's allocation the primary metric never becomes readable
findings.evidence: detecting a 50% relative lift at the 3% field rate needs 2,515 accounts per arm. At 15 per arm per weekly cycle that is 168 weeks (3.2 years) — longer than the previous scoring effort survived before it lost credibility
findings.action: Assign the whole batch, not a third of it: 97 accounts per arm per cycle (291 of the 300) makes the readout land in two quarters. If the manager will not commit that volume, say so now and report only the weekly bets — do not promise a lift number that the design cannot deliver.
findings.cost: no new rep hours — the same accounts are being worked, they are being recorded as assigned rather than left out of the experiment
findings.expect: the north star becomes reachable within the horizon anyone will wait, instead of being quoted as a plan nobody can hold you to

findings.what: account_type carries no information — and if 'Suspect' means 'no engagement', it is wrong on 85% of rows
findings.evidence: the brief lists the three values and does not define them; the usual funnel reading (Suspect = no engagement yet) is OUR hypothesis. Under it, 341 of 402 training 'Suspects' and 86 of 101 scoring ones are mislabelled — they have an MQL, a trial or a contact. Under ANY reading the field is empty: conversion is identical across the three types (chi2 p = 0.84), model importance 0.003

findings.cost: one bulk update + one validation rule
findings.expect: the VP stops seeing 'Suspects' near the top of a list and losing trust in it

findings.what: Trials with zero active users are ambiguous
findings.evidence: 19 scoring accounts started a trial and show 0 active users; in training these convert at 11.0% (8 of 73), better than trials with 1-2 users
findings.action: Ask product whether these are provisioned-but-never-used or missing seat telemetry. If telemetry, instrument it — the field is currently unreadable.
findings.cost: one question to product; instrumentation if it is the second
findings.expect: a real signal becomes readable instead of being two different things in one field

findings.what: web_touchpoints_90d cannot distinguish 'no visits' from 'not measured'
findings.evidence: 103 scoring accounts show 0; in training, 0 converts at 7.4% vs 4.5% for 1-3 (Fisher p = 0.119 — directional, not established)
findings.action: Data contract with the attribution vendor: return NULL when no measurement was taken. Until then, treat 0 as unknown rather than as a measured zero.
findings.expect: a 40%-coverage problem stops being invisible because it looks like data

findings.what: It is unknown whether sales_contacts_90d precedes the outcome window or overlaps it
findings.evidence: sales_contacts_90d is a 90-day count and the label is 'converted within 90 days'. Nothing in the files states the relationship. This is the only feature with credible signal (OR 2.2 at >=4, robust to every adjustment)
findings.action: One question to the data owner: does the contact window PRECEDE the snapshot, or is it the same 90 days in which conversion is measured? If it overlaps, the one signal in this dataset is leakage and nothing built on it is real.
findings.expect: either the exploit arm is justified, or the whole dataset is known to be unusable

findings.evidence: audit §2: in-sample AUC 0.759 sits at the median of what the same architecture scores on random labels (p = 0.575); out-of-fold 0.573; forward in time 0.474, below chance

findings.expect: the next model cannot die quietly the way this one did

┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
│ AGENT · experiment_card   [template]
│ purpose     : Write the week's allocation as an experiment the manager can approve or refuse
│ sensitivity : aggregate
│ routed to   : cloud
│ reads       : arms (name, size, selection rule), matching variables, base rate, readout date
│ returns     : markdown, ~150 words
├─ SYSTEM ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
│ You write experiment cards for an SDR manager who is not technical and
│ is sceptical of being experimented on. Be concrete about what each arm
│ is testing and what result would make us stop. Never oversell, and never
│ promise a lift number we do not have.
├─ PROMPT ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
│ This week's allocation splits 90 accounts into 3 matched arms
│ (intent segment and contact band). Base rate is 6.5% in training, 1-3% per the business.
│ 
│ - **continue** (45 accounts): 1–4 logged contacts, trial > vendor record > no signal, most contacts first
│ - **first-call** (15 accounts): never contacted, trial first (half called, half observed — that is how the +10 gets measured for real), then vendor record
│ - **control** (30 accounts): the rep picks — what would happen without the system
│ - **ask** (23, not an arm): 5+ contacts, no result — the rep gets a question
│ - **observe** (13, not an arm): the other half of the untouched trials, deliberately not called
│ - **skip** (74, not an arm): web-only or MQL-only — calling never helped on any cut
│ 
│ Write the experiment card the SDR manager reads before approving. For each arm state the
│ hypothesis in one sentence, the result that would confirm it, and the result that would
│ kill it. End with the readout date and one sentence on why the control arm exists.
├─ RETURNS (worked example) ───────────────────────────────────────────────
│ **This week: 90 accounts — continue 45, first-call 15, control 30 — plus a holdout nobody calls.**
│ 
│ **continue (45)** — Hypothesis: the best information we hold — a prospect who stated readiness, then 1–4 logged contacts with a trial, then with a vendor record, then by count — beats the model's score. Confirms: converts at or above control. Kills: converts below control once both arms pass 2,500 accounts.
│ 
│ **first-call (15)** — Hypothesis: the first call on an untouched trial account is where an hour changes most (+10 pts on history, an upper bound). Half are called, half observed. Confirms: called converts above observed. Kills: no difference at 138 per group.
│ 
│ **control (30)** — The rep picks. This is what happens without the system, and it is the only reason either arm above can be read.
│ 
│ **ask** — 5+ contacts, no result, no conversation on file. The rep gets one question, not a call: what do you know that the data does not? Their answer decides whether the account rests or returns.
│ 
│ **holdout** — Prospects who said no after 4+ contacts and agreed to no next step. Nobody calls them. If they convert anyway, the extractor misread them.
│ 
│ First readout 2026-10-30. It will be noisy — 30 per arm cannot resolve a realistic difference — and it accumulates. The control arm exists because Cordilla has never had one, which is why nobody could write up how the last scoring effort died.

actions.action: Assign the whole batch, not a third of it: 97 accounts per arm per cycle (291 of the 300) makes the readout land in two quarters. If the manager will not commit that volume, say so now and report only the weekly bets — do not promise a lift number that the design cannot deliver.
actions.cost: no new rep hours — the same accounts are being worked, they are being recorded as assigned rather than left out of the experiment
actions.expect: the north star becomes reachable within the horizon anyone will wait, instead of being quoted as a plan nobody can hold you to

actions.what: Trials with zero active users are ambiguous
actions.evidence: 19 scoring accounts started a trial and show 0 active users; in training these convert at 11.0% (8 of 73), better than trials with 1-2 users
actions.action: Ask product whether these are provisioned-but-never-used or missing seat telemetry. If telemetry, instrument it — the field is currently unreadable.
actions.cost: one question to product; instrumentation if it is the second
actions.expect: a real signal becomes readable instead of being two different things in one field

actions.what: web_touchpoints_90d cannot distinguish 'no visits' from 'not measured'
actions.evidence: 103 scoring accounts show 0; in training, 0 converts at 7.4% vs 4.5% for 1-3 (Fisher p = 0.119 — directional, not established)
actions.action: Data contract with the attribution vendor: return NULL when no measurement was taken. Until then, treat 0 as unknown rather than as a measured zero.
actions.expect: a 40%-coverage problem stops being invisible because it looks like data
